atoms.a: Why do you think people originally took trips to the seaside?

feedback.end: In the 1800s, people believed that the sea had the power to cure illness. Before trains were common, rich people took long journeys to the beach in horse-drawn coaches to restore their health.

instruction.text: Select the image of the seaside.

feedback.end: During the 1900s, more train lines were built between coastal towns and cities, so the seaside became a very popular holiday destination.

trainers.instruction: What do you think the “Holidays with Pay Act” forced employers to do? Select the correct answer.

cards.text: give their workers 1 week of paid holiday
cards.sound: give their workers 1 week of paid holiday

feedback.finish: After the act was passed in 1938, seaside holidays also became affordable among workers and their families across Britain.

atoms.b: Many coastal towns in England became well known for their tourism. They became ((++seaside jungle)) resorts.
In the South of England, people went to Brighton, Eastbourne and Margate to enjoy the beach. Brighton’s Palace Pier had regular ((++theatre fishing)) performances and family entertainment.

hint.label: Pier
hint.text: A pier is a platform on pillars stretching out into the sea.

atoms.b: Blackpool also became a large seaside resort. It had lots of visitors from factory towns in the North. The Central Pier was used for outdoor ((++dancing skiing)) until the arrival of fairground rides in the mid 1900s.

instruction.text: Listen and read along with the postcard. Select all the different seaside activities that are mentioned.

hint.text: Punch and Judy is a puppet show that was often performed to entertain children at the beach.
hint.label: Punch and Judy

atoms.a: Hi Gran! We had the most exciting day in Blackpool. I won the sandcastle competition and watched a punch and judy show. Mum and dad relaxed on the deck chairs while we had a donkey ride in the evening.

instruction.text: Select one of the cars to find out about one of Blackpool’s popular attractions.

feedback.finish: Blackpool is home to an amusement park known as the Pleasure Beach. In 1907, the park opened its first wooden roller coaster, which was named The Scenic Railway.

atoms.a: How many people do you think visit the Pleasure Beach every year nowadays?
